messages:
Dmitri: Heads-up — eu-west GPU pools just hit sustained 95% util, queue depth x3 since 10:12 UTC. Autoscaler couldn't provision because we hit regional quota. Seeing p95 gen latency creep to ~600ms and some OOM evictions.
Kevin: Ugh. Are we spilling to other regions right now?
Dmitri: Not automatically. Current policy blocks cross-region unless emergency flag set. Proposal: enable controlled spill to us-east but only via model-fallback and an admit controller. Instead of blunt spill, use "admit tokens" based on free slot budget and model cost. Tokens say which model tier to accept and max-latency budget.
Sara: +1 for controlled approach. Two quick asks: 1) data residency opt-outs for customers; 2) prefer same-region quantized fallback before cross-region.
Maria: For the on-call runbook, I'd do: 1) warm up us-east warmpool for the affected model, 2) enable model-fallback chain (large->medium-q8->small-q4), 3) start auction-admit with weights for paid tiers, 4) monitor token_drain and cancel after 10m if no drop.
Dmitri: sample admit policy sketch (not prod):
```json
{
  "admit_window_s": 10,
  "tokens_per_window": 120,
  "weights": {
    "enterprise": 0.6,
    "paid": 0.3,
    "free": 0.1
  },
  "fallback_order": ["gpt-large-v1","gpt-medium-q8","gpt-small-q4"],
  "max_cross_region_ratio": 0.2
}
```
Kevin: Two concerns: egress cost (us-east) and cold-start tail if we spin up many small models. Can we bias tokens to same-region low-quant fallback first? Also prefer throttling API keys that exceed their SLA rather than global shed.
Sara: Also flag for network path quality — if cross-region RTT spikes >100ms we should stop spilling and instead shed to cheaper fallback locally.
Maria: Agree. Add a grace_period metric so we don't oscillate: only allow spill if sustained high queue for 30s and only disable after 3 minutes of recovery.
Dmitri: Putting together a minimal implementation: - admit-controller service that watches per-region free_slots, issues tokens to request router; - router consumes token, picks model from fallback_order encoded in token; - billing tags in token to bias weight. I'll open a tiny PR for the admit-controller interface.
ops-bot: @deploy-bot scheduled deploy: admit-controller v0.1 to staging at 15:30 UTC (dry-run). :rocket:
oncall: tagging @oncall for visibility — please watch token_drain and queue_length metrics in the next run.
oncall: I can't actually tag, but please ping the on-call rotation if you need manual override.
Kevin: Sounds reasonable. If staging looks good, let's roll to canary with 1% traffic and strict observability (token_accept_rate, cross_region_egress_bytes, p99+p95 latency per-model).
Maria: I'll update the runbook with the exact steps and add the cost calculator snippet to estimate egress + model delta per 1k requests.
Dmitri: Thanks — PR in a bit. If anyone has objections to the token semantics (time-limited, non-transferable, contains model_hint + budget) speak up now.
Kevin: No objections. small nit: persist token rejection reasons for triage (quota, residency, rtt).
Sara: I'm good. Oncall team: please stand by for dry-run telemetry.
Maria: tagging ops Slack channel with the playbook once PR merges. :white_check_mark:
